data.short_meaning: Sky Splitter, Ruler of the Sky
data.long_meaning: Vyomasena is a name derived from Sanskrit, which means 'Sky Splitter' or 'Ruler of the Sky'. He is a central character in Hindu mythology, often depicted as the elder brother of the god Vayu (the wind god). The name Vyomasena carries the meaning “Sky Splitter, Ruler of the Sky” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Vyomasena usually hope their child will grow to embody sky splitter, ruler of the sky and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Vyomasena total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: Vyomasena has significant cultural significance in Hindu mythology as he is often pictured riding on his chariot pulled by horses or elephants. He is also associated with the planet Saturn and is revered especially in Jyotish (Indian Astrology). This name holds great importance in many Hindu communities and is often invoked during rituals and festivals associated with the planets.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Vyomasena carries deep spiritual significance in Hinduism. As a divine being, he is believed to have the power to create and control the cosmos, especially the sky. It symbolizes the limitless potential and power that lies within each one of us. It serves as a reminder that no matter how vast and infinite the universe may be, each one of us has the ability to transcend our individual boundaries and truly realize our divine potential. Additionally, as his name suggests, he represents the potential to split open one's own limitations and expand one's consciousness to the infinite.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Vyomasena: Master of the cosmic elements. Symbolizes the supreme control over the five fundamental elements of nature - Earth, Water, Fire, Air, and Space.

historical_references.reference: Vyomasena is mentioned in the Indian epic Mahabharata as the king of the Gandharvas, a race of celestial beings. He is described as a powerful warrior and magician, who is an ally of the Pandavas and plays a crucial role in the Kurukshetra War.

Another reference to Vyomasena comes from the Puranas, where he is described as the son of the god Indra and the apsara Menaka. He is also known as the king of the Nagas (serpent beings), and is said to possess the power to control the elements and manipulate space itself.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Vyomasena' from Hindu mythology has gained modern relevance beyond religious and mythological contexts. It is often used as a character name in Indian comic books, reflecting the integration of Indian mythology into popular culture. In Hindi cinema, 'Vyomasena' is used as a name for characters in science fiction and fantasy films, showcasing the influence of mythology on the genre. On social media, the name is used as a handle or username by individuals, often in a humorous or reverential way, highlighting the enduring appeal of Hindu mythology in contemporary culture.
